drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. 56-year-old female admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.59, creatinine 2.03-2.19, hemoglobin 13, platelets 309-311, sodium 138-139, wbc 9.2-9.3; vitals dbp 65-71, heart_rate 71-74, map 85-89, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-17, sbp 122-126, spo2 97-98, temp 36.8-36.9
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Chronic kidney disease stage 3. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Acute renal failure.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 2.36-2.52, hemoglobin 12.8-12.9, platelets 310-315, sodium 139, wbc 8.9-9; vitals dbp 65-70, heart_rate 70-75, map 84-88, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-17, sbp 123-127, spo2 97-99, temp 36.7-36.9
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Hold lisinopril; Lactated Ringer's 1 L IV bolus
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Chronic kidney disease stage 3. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Acute renal failure. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 56-year-old female, length of stay 5 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Chronic kidney disease stage 3. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Acute renal failure. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient seen and examined at bedside.
